purpose: #1150 operating-cost refactor: classify the existing npm/script validation surface without deleting gates. The manifest is intentionally additive; future cleanup PRs must keep required gates classified before retiring wrappers.

rules.note: Default release/test/build gates and their direct self-check helpers must stay classified as required gates.
Public-readiness, source-public, monorepo transition, and repo-protection checks are standard gated validation surfaces.
A2A routing, dispatch, finalizer, worker readiness, and team-round scripts stay visible as standard validation surfaces.
Test and documentation check helpers are not deletion candidates unless a replacement gate is documented.

CI-consumed gates misclassified by the catch-all: check:approval-records runs in ci.yml and check:source-quality-floors is wired into the core release-gate tier and package CI parity. #1503 Wave 0 classification fix.
Catch-all keeps legacy/manual scripts classified so future PRs must explicitly justify retirement.
Broker build/test/TCK/inventory scripts define the default package validation surface.
#1503 Wave 2: 24 rollout/preflight aliases collapsed into the rollout dispatcher (scripts/rollout-preflight-manifest.json). scan:public-readiness stays direct (package CI parity requiredScript).

#1503 Wave 1: the 59 terminal-brief approval aliases collapsed into the terminal_brief dispatcher (scripts/terminal-brief-manifest.json). The dispatcher stays approval-gated; per-tool wrappers remain approval boundaries and must not be bulk-deleted.

#1503 Wave 2: the 21 orchestration-intelligence aliases collapsed into the orchestration dispatcher (scripts/orchestration-manifest.json). Wrappers remain approval boundaries and must not be bulk-deleted.
A2A round, finalizer, classifier, routing, and parent-aggregate scripts remain explicit validation surfaces.
Diagnostics and local development scripts are manual surfaces and should not be mistaken for default release gates.
Catch-all keeps uncategorized broker scripts visible for later caller-audit review rather than silent deletion.
